question.text: An ideal gas undergoes isothermal compression from <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>5</mn><mi mathvariant="normal"> </mi><msup><mi mathvariant="normal">m</mi><mn>3</mn></msup></math> to <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>1</mn><mi mathvariant="normal"> </mi><msup><mi mathvariant="normal">m</mi><mn>3</mn></msup></math> against a constant external pressure of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>4</mn><mi mathvariant="normal"> </mi><mi mathvariant="normal">N</mi><mo> </mo><msup><mi mathvariant="normal">m</mi><mrow><mo>-</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow></msup></math>. The heat released in this process is <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>24</mn><mi mathvariant="normal"> </mi><mi mathvariant="normal">J</mi><mi mathvariant="normal"> </mi><msup><mi>mol</mi><mrow><mo>-</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup><msup><mi mathvariant="normal">K</mi><mrow><mo>-</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup></math> and is used to increase the pressure of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>1</mn></math> mole of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>Al</mi></math>. The temperature of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>Al</mi></math> increases by:

solution.text:
Work done on isothermal irreversible compression for an ideal gas:

W=-4 1-5=16 J

For an isothermal process,∆U=0

q=-16J; heat released is 16 J.

q=nCmΔT

16=1×24×∆T

∆T=23 K
